reports.headline: Seoul forum confrontation is not a maritime attack
reports.text: New September 8 Korean press headlines cover Philippine defence chief's clash with Chinese delegates at Seoul forum. Diplomatic confrontation is not a verified armed maritime incident; hold.

reports.headline: Iran referral remains draft; inspection gap persists
reports.text: IAEA full September 7 statement confirms no declared-facility information or in-field access during reporting period. September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters confirms E3/US referral draft is still unsubmitted and wording remains unsettled. No new 90-percent enrichment or nuclear test verified; retain existing access-gap signal.

reports.headline: Zaporizhzhia repair arrangement is not grid restoration
reports.text: HISTORICAL September 7 pre-restoration assessment. Superseded by Energoatom-attributed September 7 evening restoration reported in full by Hromadske on September 8. IAEA September 7 statement directly verifies diesel dependence since August 20 and localized weekend ceasefire for power-line repairs. Work expected to finish is not restored off-site electricity. New September 8 strike tallies remain attributed/index-only; hold.

reports.headline: AP verifies Kfar Rumman toll; existing truce violation reinforced
reports.text: AP full report via PBS verifies September 7 Kfar Rumman strikes: Health Ministry reports at least 12 killed, including two children. Israeli military attributes strikes to drone attacks; Hezbollah did not claim them. Existing truce-violation evidence strengthened, not a new numerical increment; prisoner exchange remains prior context.

reports.headline: Fresh piracy reporting describes earlier hijackings
reports.text: September 8 Guardian original full article retrieved by terminal HTTP and Responsible Statecraft analysis document piracy resurgence and earlier April-August hijackings. Fresh structural reporting, not a separately established September 8 seizure; hold and monitor maritime incident notices.

reports.headline: Destroyer commissioning is not a new weapons test
reports.text: Reuters full text confirms Kang Kon commissioning occurred Sunday September 6. Kim calls it part of nuclear response system but KCNA does not establish nuclear weapons aboard. Official DVIDS confirms allied Freedom Edge opening September 7. Neither is a newly verified DPRK missile-range or nuclear test; hold.

reports.headline: Sabotage arrests relate to August energy-site attacks
reports.text: September 7 Turkiye Today full text says GNU announced September 6 arrests of five suspects over attacks in first half of August. New investigation reporting, not a fresh refinery strike; hold. Broader index adds UN roadmap and French engagement coverage.

reports.headline: Quintet mission scheduled to begin; no outcome confirmed
reports.text: Official EEAS confirms planned September 8-10 AU/IGAD/Arab League/EU/UN consultations in Khartoum. UN September 7 civilian-harm warning appears in past-day index. No completed mission or ceasefire established; hold.

reports.headline: Oil near $97 reflects supply risk, not nuclear odds
reports.text: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

reports.headline: Iran UN-referral push remains a draft, not an adopted decision
reports.text: September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters says E3 and US seek support for referral; draft not formally submitted and wording remains unsettled. Baghaei threatens unspecified necessary measures. Continuing inspection gap corroborated; no newly verified enrichment measurement or nuclear test.

reports.headline: Manila reports unchanged US commitments despite regional drill concerns
reports.text: September 7 Reuters interview, retrieved via AsiaOne, quotes Teodoro warning China may exploit gaps but reporting definite US treaty assurances and no reduction in US-Philippine military activities. This is an allied-position update, not an observed new clash.

reports.headline: Reuters corroborates Norway warning; launcher delivery was in August
reports.text: September 7 Reuters confirms Moscow warning over US missile launchers, strategic-dialogue criticism and conditional wartime targeting. Delivery predates the statement. No observed nuclear alert change or explicit nuclear-use threat is established.

reports.headline: Myanmar corridor fighting warrants follow-up; full detail unavailable
reports.text: September 8 Nikkei headline and opening material report intensified operations around Chinese economic-corridor projects and civilian displacement. Full operational details not retrieved, so new publication is not assigned as new offensive onset. Hold score pending corroboration.

reports.headline: New Haiti analysis highlights rural gang expansion, not a new-day massacre
reports.text: September 7 Reuters full text cites GI-TOC findings on mobile rural raids, roadblocks, kidnappings and worsening Artibonite insecurity. Kenscoff is a recent example; exact attack onset is not established as today. Structural warning strengthened without automatic probability increment.

reports.headline: Official release confirms Freedom Edge has begun
reports.text: DVIDS confirms September 7 opening with Japan, Republic of Korea and United States; runs September 7-11. This resolves prior index-only start confirmation, not evidence of a DPRK weapons test.

reports.headline: Mandera reports separated: September 6 assault versus July recirculation
reports.text: Direct Kenyans.co.ke article 126850 dates Arabia Town attack to September 6, casualties unconfirmed. Article 125576 recirculating in September concerns July Fino/Arabia attacks, explicitly distinguished by newer article and July 25 Xinhua. Newer assault is not verified fresh mobilization or infrastructure-strike signal. Hold; correct source dating.

reports.headline: IAEA: verification gap persists; Gulf radiation remains at background levels
reports.text: September 7 IAEA full statement verifies no information or facility access in reporting period and lost inventory continuity for over a year. This supports existing access-denial assessment, not a verified new 90% enrichment or nuclear test. Gulf radiation reported at normal background levels. Hold.

reports.headline: Hormuz corridor remains proposed; shipping has not stopped
reports.text: September 7 Reuters full text confirms proposed restricted zone/corridor, not implementation or zero traffic. Ten commodity transits daily on ten-day average; US energy secretary separately claims flows recovering. Weekend tanker strikes and conditional retaliation remain prior-window context. No new minefield or bomber deployment independently verified; hold.

reports.headline: Qalibaf warns US-linked Gulf energy assets are exposed
reports.text: September 7 Yeni Safak, citing Anadolu and Qalibaf, reports a conditional warning against US-linked Gulf oil and gas assets if Iranian assets are struck. This corroborates the existing energy threat, not an observed new facility attack. Later Reuters headline indexed; full article unavailable.

reports.headline: CPJ documents journalist injuries across Lebanon and Gaza
reports.text: CPJ reports two Lebanese journalists and a Gaza journalist injured on September 6; another Gaza injury was two weeks earlier. September 7 publication is new corroborating reporting, not four new-day injuries or a separate probability increment.

reports.headline: UN rights warning highlights expanding drone harm
reports.text: Radio Tamazuj reports September 7 UN rights calls to halt fighting and foreign involvement, with rising civilian danger across Kordofan, Blue Nile and Darfur. Casualty examples in the report are not established as new-day attacks. Quintet September 8-10 mission remains prospective.

reports.headline: Haiti rural-expansion reporting traced to September 4 analysis
reports.text: Fresh Reuters-indexed coverage points to a structural shift outside Port-au-Prince. Original GI-TOC analysis is dated September 4 and describes the August 23 Kenscoff attack. Do not count the recirculated massacre as a fresh September event.
sources: Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime

reports.headline: Quintet confirms September 8–10 Khartoum political mission
reports.text: New official EEAS Quintet statement confirms planned September 8–10 Khartoum good-offices mission with AU, IGAD, Arab League, EU and UN; coordination with Quad. Scheduled political consultations, not an agreed ceasefire or completed mission. No numerical change.

reports.headline: Norway launcher warning corroborated; no verified nuclear alert
reports.text: September 7 AeroTime full report and Anadolu search corroborate attributed Russian warning that Norway launcher infrastructure is a wartime target and undermines strategic dialogue. Russian official page extraction failed; secondary sources retained. August 27 launcher delivery is not a new deployment today; no explicit nuclear-use threat or fresh alert verified. Hold.

reports.headline: Gaza ministry reports five killed in preceding 24 hours
reports.text: Direct September 7 Al Jazeera reports Gaza ministry tally of five killed and thirty injured over preceding 24 hours, with two further deaths from earlier wounds. Dates span September 6–7; attributed casualty reporting, no independently isolated additional operational threshold. Hold inherited score, not calm.

reports.headline: Full IAEA statement verifies continuing Iran safeguards access gap
reports.text: The September 7 prepared Board statement says the Agency received neither facility-status information nor in-field access in the reporting period. It lost continuity of knowledge of previously declared uranium inventories up to 60% over a year ago. This resolves the earlier full-source access gap; it does not establish new enrichment, a weapon or an adopted referral.

reports.headline: IAEA: repair ceasefire underway; grid restoration not yet confirmed
reports.text: Grossi says the seventh local arrangement took hold over the weekend, allowing demining and line repairs. Emergency diesel has powered the site since August 20; cooling pumps operated intermittently as fuel depleted. Repairs expected shortly is not confirmation of restored electricity.

reports.headline: Lebanon toll updated to 12 in AFP report
reports.text: AFP now cites the Lebanese health ministry reporting 11 killed in one Kfar Rumman building strike and a rescuer killed in another attack. Earlier Reuters reporting gave at least 11. This updates the same overnight violence, not a separate score increment.

reports.headline: Nigeria truce investigation concerns June-origin arrangement
reports.text: The New Humanitarian reports a Boko Haram truce operating since June and possible extension, based on three contacts. Government and military did not respond before publication; ISWAP is excluded. New reporting does not establish a newly signed nationwide settlement. Await corroboration; score held.

reports.headline: Russia warns over Norway launcher; deployment predates today
reports.text: AeroTime attributes a September 7 wartime-target warning to Zakharova. The launcher arrived August 27 for an exercise ending September 4; published US material does not specify accompanying munitions. No explicit nuclear-use threat or changed nuclear alert is established here.
sources: AeroTime citing Russian statements and US/Norwegian releases

reports.headline: IAEA resolves Syria past-nuclear safeguards questions
reports.text: Grossi reports that Syrian information and access allowed outstanding past-nuclear safeguards issues to be clarified and resolved. This is national safeguards progress, not proof of Idlib battlefield de-escalation; the existing regional tracker is held.

reports.headline: Fresh Grossi access headlines await full-statement verification
reports.text: September 7 news indexes report prolonged lack of access to Iranian sites. Official Board schedule is verified, but the full opening statement could not be retrieved. Not confirmation of a new enrichment measurement, detonation or adopted referral.
sources: Google News index; IAEA meeting advisory

reports.headline: Mandera date mismatch: direct article says Friday, not Monday dawn
reports.text: A September 7 indexed attack headline led to a direct article describing Friday evening attacks in Fino and Arabia. A social post instead says Monday dawn. Event date is unresolved; do not count a fresh Monday attack.

reports.headline: Kang Kon commissioning is not a newly verified missile or nuclear test
reports.text: Reuters reports the warship was formally deployed September 6 and Kim described a nuclear response role. Actual weapons aboard were unspecified. The current configured test signals are not established by commissioning alone.

reports.headline: Manila pairs alliance-gap warning with US security assurances
reports.text: Teodoro warns China could exploit reduced US-South Korean drills, but reports definite US commitments to Manila. Freedom Edge trilateral drills are scheduled September 7-11; Seoul has not decided on a Hormuz deployment.

reports.headline: Reuters reports at least 11 killed in overnight Kfar Rumman strikes
reports.text: Reuters September 7 cites Lebanon's NNA: overnight building and vehicle strikes killed at least 11, including two children and two medics. Separate from Sunday's toll. Existing truce-violation assessment corroborated; no score increase.

reports.headline: Iran outlines proposed Gulf restricted zone; implementation not verified
reports.text: Reuters September 7 reports future restricted-zone and corridor maps, with signature expected in coming days. Kpler records ten daily commodity transits on a ten-day average. Severe disruption is not zero traffic.

reports.headline: Event-date check: Kenscoff 47-death attack occurred in August
reports.text: Past-day index recirculates a 47-death Haiti headline. Direct August 27 Al Jazeera/AP coverage dates the mass kidnapping and attack to August 23. Not counted as a newly verified September massacre.

reports.headline: Niger mutiny review distinguishes allegation from verified intervention
reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/Reuters review dates the failed mutiny to August 29. Niger alleges French orchestration; France denies it. No newly established French military intervention and no duplicate theatre added.

reports.headline: Hormuz traffic at lowest since May, but not zero
reports.text: Reuters' September 7 dateline cites Kpler: ten commodity ships per day on a ten-day average; two passed Saturday and six Sunday. No VLCC had exited since Wednesday. This strengthens evidence of severe shipping disruption without establishing a complete closure.
sources: Reuters citing Kpler, LSEG and UKMTO

reports.headline: Manila warns of alliance gaps; US assurances remain
reports.text: September 7 Al Jazeera/AP/Reuters reports Teodoro's warning that China may exploit reduced US-South Korean exercises. He also cites definite US assurances to Manila. Five-day Freedom Edge drills are due to begin today; South Korean Hormuz contributions remain undecided.

reports.headline: Libya announces arrests over older energy-facility attacks
reports.text: Anadolu reports the unity government's Sunday announcement that five suspects were arrested. The article explicitly dates the underlying drone attacks to early August. This is a new investigative announcement, not a newly verified attack.
sources: Anadolu citing Government of National Unity

reports.headline: Kang Kon joins fleet; actual nuclear load unspecified
reports.text: Reuters confirms Sunday's commissioning and Kim's description of the destroyer as part of a nuclear response system. The report does not specify nuclear weapons aboard. No qualifying new test is established; score held.
sources: Reuters via SRN News, citing KCNA

reports.headline: UN confirms September 8 Quintet meetings; no Monday briefing
reports.text: The browser-verified September 4 UN briefing schedules envoy and Quintet meetings in Khartoum for September 8. It also says there will be no September 7 noon briefing because of Labor Day. These are scheduled contacts, not a signed settlement.

reports.headline: Reuters confirms Sunday destroyer commissioning and nuclear-role rhetoric
reports.text: Reuters, citing KCNA, dates Kang Kon commissioning to September 6. Kim describes a nuclear-response role, but nuclear weapons aboard are unspecified. US, South Korea and Japan begin Freedom Edge on September 7. Neither configured test trigger is established; score held.
sources: Reuters via WMBD; KCNA and South Korean JCS attributed

reports.headline: AP corroborates planned exclusion zone; implementation unverified
reports.text: AP September 6 directly corroborates Rezaei's planned exclusion-zone announcement. Coordinates and implementation remain unclear, and the US denies the claimed vessel hit. Attributed oil-transit estimates conflict with tracking averages; no confirmed zero traffic.

reports.headline: OPEC directly confirms October production hold
reports.text: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

reports.headline: Taiwan patrol investigation describes a campaign dating to June
reports.text: Direct Bloomberg syndication reports east-coast patrols averaging two cutters monthly since June. Taiwan coast guard response and US criticism are included. The September publication does not establish a new blockade or invasion; hold without double-counting in South China Sea.

reports.headline: Envoys cite progress, but no settlement; plant power remains critical
reports.text: September 6 Kyiv Post reports US envoys seeking renewed trilateral talks after meetings with Zelensky and European advisers. IAEA Update 365 confirms repair arrangements but continued diesel and cooling vulnerability. Diplomatic progress claims are not a signed peace deal; nuclear safety is distinct from weapons use.

reports.headline: AFP confirms rising days-long Yemen toll and displacement
reports.text: AFP September 6 reports more than 300 combatants and some civilians killed in days of fighting, with journalists observing displaced families. A reported Taiz-Mokha road cutoff increases maritime-access concern but does not prove complete strait closure. Existing score held.

reports.headline: Iran announces planned maritime restriction beyond Hormuz
reports.text: Anadolu reports Rezaei says a restricted zone will be declared in coming days and an Oman corridor agreement is planned. His complete-closure and missile-test claims are unverified; announcement is not implementation. No new closure signal.

reports.headline: New Deir al-Zahrani evacuation warning follows deadly Sunday strikes
reports.text: Anadolu reports an early-Monday Israeli warning before a planned strike in Deir al-Zahrani. Reuters separately confirms seven killed Sunday, citing Lebanon's health ministry. Warning is not confirmation of a completed strike; existing ceasefire-violation signal held.

reports.headline: Yemen fighting toll exceeds 300; government reports tanker interception
reports.text: AFP reports more than 300 combatants and some civilians killed over several days, with displacement witnessed by its journalists. Anadolu relays a Coast Guard account that tanker Nerida was intercepted after a Ras Isa delivery and gunfire; no casualties reported. No verified strait closure; score held.

reports.headline: Kyiv talks include allied consultation; nuclear-plant power remains key trigger
reports.text: Anadolu confirms September 6 talks with US envoys; Ukrainian side says British, French and German advisers join expanded format. No peace agreement verified. IAEA Update 365 warns dwindling diesel and intermittent cooling make off-site power restoration urgent, a nuclear-safety risk rather than weapons-use evidence.

reports.headline: Libya announces sabotage-cell arrests linked to August attacks
reports.text: Anadolu relays GNU announcement of five arrests over drone attacks on Tripoli and Zawiya energy facilities. The cited attacks occurred in the first half of August. New arrest statement is not a new infrastructure strike; hold.

reports.headline: Iranian Erbil aerostat claim refers to an earlier strike
reports.text: Anadolu reports IRGC claims an aerostat was destroyed near Erbil during Wednesday's clashes; no immediate US comment. September 6 publication does not make this a new attack. Uncorroborated claim held below activation threshold.

reports.headline: Lebanon death toll rises to seven; Aoun seeks US intervention
reports.text: September 6 AFP via Dawn updates the death toll to at least seven, citing Lebanon's health ministry, including three in a separate Nabatieh al-Tahta drone strike. Aoun appeals for US intervention. Existing ceasefire violation persists; hold saturated score.

reports.headline: Wright downplays nuclear-deal prospects; referral remains proposed
reports.text: AP and direct draft-resolution reporting confirm US/E3 referral effort, not adopted UN action. September 6 Wright interview reporting downplays prospects for a signed deal; pessimism is not an explicit new refusal. No fresh verified weapons-grade enrichment or nuclear test; hold.

reports.headline: US disputes Iranian vessel-hit claim; oil transit estimates remain contested
reports.text: AP September 6 confirms US denial of an alleged unmanned-vessel hit and US acknowledgment of September 5 tanker strikes. Wright's 9 million barrels/day transit figure is attributed and exceeds longer-period tracking estimates. No verified total closure or zero traffic; hold.

reports.headline: Kyiv diplomacy continues alongside critical nuclear-plant power risk
reports.text: Reuters photo caption and DW/agency reporting corroborate September 6 Kyiv visit by US envoys; European advisers reportedly participate. No settlement verified. IAEA Update 365 directly confirms repair ceasefire and diesel/cooling vulnerability; nuclear safety is not weapons use. Hold.

reports.headline: Somalia issues piracy warning; cited rescue dates to August 29
reports.text: Eastleigh Voice September 6 directly reports Somali government piracy warning and international-cooperation appeal. Incidents date from April; MV Lutuf liberation dated August 29. New statement is not a new hijacking. Hold; no signal change.

reports.headline: Reuters reports US envoys met Zelenskyy; no settlement confirmed
reports.text: September 6 Reuters search snippet reports envoys met Zelenskyy in Kyiv, corroborated by BBC news index; full Reuters syndication timed out. Existing diplomacy_active held, no peace deal confirmed. IAEA Update 365 directly confirms repair ceasefire and critical diesel/off-site-power risk, not weapons use.
sources: Reuters search excerpt; BBC news index

reports.headline: AP: US denies vessel-hit claim; oil-flow estimate remains attributed
reports.text: AP September 6 directly confirms US denial of the alleged unmanned-vessel hit and acknowledged September 5 tanker strikes. Wright estimates 9 million barrels/day transit; AP notes estimate exceeds tracking averages. No verified zero traffic or total closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Lebanon reports four killed in dawn strikes; pullback not approved
reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP directly reports at least four killed and 20 wounded, citing Lebanese authorities; Israel attributes strikes to Hezbollah drones. Qatar urges de-escalation. Pullback plan remains unapproved. Hold.

reports.headline: US rejects Iran claim of a vessel hit; damage remains unverified
reports.text: AP September 6 confirms the US explicitly denies Iran's claimed hit on an unmanned vessel. September 5 US tanker strikes remain acknowledged. Wright's ABC interview reports substantial but restricted oil transit; no verified zero traffic or total Hormuz closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Wright says nuclear agreement may not happen; no technical threshold verified
reports.text: September 6 ABC transcript: Wright says a nuclear agreement may not occur and emphasizes destroying capabilities. This is a policy statement, not confirmed enrichment, weapons development or a formal refusal of talks. IAEA confirms regular Board meeting September 7; US/E3 referral effort is not adopted action. Hold.

reports.headline: IAEA regular Board opens September 7; agenda is not a resolution
reports.text: IAEA schedules Board opening at 10:00 CEST September 7 and Grossi press conference at 12:30 CEST. Iran, DPRK and Ukraine are on the agenda. This is a regular scheduled meeting, not evidence of emergency action or an adopted Iran referral.

reports.headline: US envoys reach Ukraine; ZNPP repair and diesel risk remain unresolved
reports.text: ABC September 6 directly reports US envoys arriving in Ukraine after Moscow talks; no settlement confirmed. IAEA Update 365 confirms local repair ceasefire, off-site power loss and dwindling diesel at ZNPP. Safety risk is distinct from nuclear-weapons use. Hold.

reports.headline: Lebanon dawn strikes confirmed; proposed pullback not approved
reports.text: Direct September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP report corroborates dawn strikes and at least four deaths attributed to Lebanese authorities. Qatar presses de-escalation. Proposed Israeli pullback is unapproved, not an implemented withdrawal. Existing ceasefire_violation corroborated; hold.

reports.headline: Western Yemen fighting continues; territorial claims remain attributed
reports.text: Direct September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP confirms intense western-front fighting and OCHA displacement. Hais recapture is a government claim, not independently verified control. No verified Bab al-Mandab closure. Hold saturated score.

reports.headline: NATO envoy backs national responses to hybrid attacks
reports.text: Reuters September 5 directly confirms US NATO envoy backs primarily national responses to hybrid attacks. Antisubmarine-exercise headlines do not establish weapons alert or Article 5. Hold.

reports.headline: Wright cites oil transit recovery; independent flow verification still needed
reports.text: ABC transcript quotes Wright putting seven-day Hormuz oil transit slightly above 9 million barrels/day, or 13-14 million including bypass pipelines. These are attributed US estimates, not an independent reopening assessment. OPEC October-hold headline remains index-only; official homepage lags at August releases.

reports.headline: Fresh Lebanon strikes corroborated in September 6 report
reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP direct report verifies fresh dawn strikes; NNA and Health Ministry report at least four killed. Israel attributes response to Hezbollah drones. Existing ceasefire_violation corroborated; hold saturated score.

reports.headline: Iran referral remains a draft, not adopted action
reports.text: Direct draft-resolution report confirms US/E3 referral proposal, not adopted Board or Security Council action. No fresh enrichment or nuclear-test threshold verified. Hold.

reports.headline: ZNPP repair ceasefire continues amid diesel risk
reports.text: IAEA Update 365 directly confirms repair ceasefire and continuing ZNPP diesel/cooling risk. September 6 BBC/NBC news indexes report US envoys arriving in Kyiv; no settlement verified. Nuclear safety is distinct from weapons use. Hold.

reports.headline: US tanker-strike acknowledgment remains central risk
reports.text: AP directly confirms US acknowledgment of three tanker strikes on September 5 and threat to Iran's oil fleet. September 6 reciprocal attack headlines remain attributed; no verified total Hormuz closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Yemen fighting persists; Hais claim remains attributed
reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP confirms continuing Taiz/Hodeidah fighting and reports OCHA displacement. Hais recapture remains government claim; no verified Bab al-Mandab closure. Existing ceasefire_violation corroborated; hold.

reports.headline: NATO envoy supports national response to hybrid attacks
reports.text: Reuters September 5 NATO envoy remarks support primarily national responses to hybrid attacks. Official NATO assistance page is July background, not a fresh deployment or nuclear alert. Hold.

reports.headline: ZNPP repair window remains urgent as diesel stocks run low
reports.text: IAEA Update 365 directly confirms local repair ceasefire, off-site power loss and diesel scarcity at ZNPP. Reuters reports Moscow talks without announced breakthrough. Nuclear-safety risk is not nuclear-weapons use. Hold.

reports.headline: Yemen western-front fighting continues; Hais control remains attributed
reports.text: Direct Al Jazeera/AFP September 6 report confirms ongoing western-front fighting and reports civilian displacement. Hais recapture remains a Yemeni military claim; no verified Bab al-Mandab closure. Hold saturated score.

reports.headline: AU engagement in Tigray confirmed; visit date unspecified
reports.text: Kenya Ministry of Defence confirms continuing AU peace-process engagement and a recent Mekelle visit but does not date the visit. Similar Reporter story is June 11, not September 5. Positive context, not a verified new timed signal; hold.

reports.headline: Tripoli depot report concerns September 3, not a new attack
reports.text: Direct Anadolu report dates suspected Tripoli depot drone to September 3; operator reported no injuries and normal fuel operations. September 5 republication is not a new attack. Hold.

reports.headline: Iran tanker strikes remain acknowledged; damage claims attributed
reports.text: AP directly confirms US acknowledgment of three tanker strikes on September 5 and threat against Iran's oil fleet. Later Iranian naval-drone and ship-hit claims remain attributed; no verified total Hormuz closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Iran referral proposal is not an adopted international decision
reports.text: US/E3 referral draft remains a proposal, not adopted IAEA or Security Council action. No newly verified enrichment, weaponization or test threshold. Access restriction carried; hold.

reports.headline: ZNPP repair ceasefire starts while diesel reserves run low
reports.text: IAEA Update 365 confirms repairs to the 330 kV line have started after demining. Off-site power has been absent since August 20; emergency generation and intermittent cooling continue. A station blackout is possible within days unless power or diesel delivery is restored. Nuclear-safety risk, not nuclear-weapons use.

reports.headline: Iran referral still a draft before regular Board meeting
reports.text: AP draft text and official IAEA calendar reviewed: E3/US referral remains unsubmitted proposal, not adopted action. Access restrictions persist per AP report; no freshly verified weapon or enrichment threshold. Hold.

reports.headline: US acknowledgment of tanker strikes remains central risk
reports.text: AP confirms US military acknowledgment of three tanker strikes and oil-fleet threat September 5. Later reciprocal-attack headlines remain attributed; no verified total traffic cessation. Hold.

reports.headline: Moscow talks end without announced breakthrough
reports.text: Reuters reports more than three hours of talks and a planned Sunday Kyiv visit. Capital-specific restraint is not a nationwide settlement.

reports.headline: NATO envoy warns against hybrid attacks
reports.text: Reuters September 5: US NATO envoy backs national responses to hybrid attacks. No new alliance combat decision or nuclear alert verified. Hold.

reports.headline: Yemen fighting continues; territorial claims contested
reports.text: September 5 direct Al Jazeera report confirms continuing western-front fighting and attributed government air attacks. September 6 Hays-control claim remains uncorroborated; effective strait closure not verified. Hold.

reports.headline: Pagoda bombardment report needs independent corroboration
reports.text: Narinjara direct HTTP fallback reports September 4 Ponnagyun pagoda bombardment, published September 5, citing locals. Single-source and outside event window; do not re-date or inflate. Hold.

reports.headline: Moscow talks confirmed useful, without breakthrough
reports.text: Reuters full report now retrieved: Kremlin calls September 5 US-envoy talks highly useful but gives no breakthrough. Capital-specific three-day restraint is not nationwide ceasefire. Existing diplomacy signal reconfirmed; hold.

reports.headline: Western referral proposal remains draft ahead of IAEA Board
reports.text: Direct report confirms US/UK/France/Germany draft referral proposal, not adoption. Official IAEA index confirms regular September 7-11 Board meeting. No fresh enrichment/test threshold; access-denial signal carried, not independently reconfirmed today.

reports.headline: Tanker strikes and oil-fleet threat remain central risk
reports.text: AP direct report confirms CENTCOM acknowledged three tanker strikes and threatened the oil fleet September 5. Damage and attack sequence remain military claims; later retaliation damage unverified. Hold.

reports.headline: Western-front fighting continues; strait closure unverified
reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 full report describes government air attacks and continued western-front fighting; reinforcement and territorial claims attributed/contested. Existing truce-breach signal reconfirmed; effective Bab al-Mandeb closure not verified. Hold.

reports.headline: Hybrid-defence warning is not a nuclear alert
reports.text: Reuters September 5 confirms US NATO envoy support for national responses to hybrid attacks; submarine-defence reporting does not establish nuclear alert or Article 5 decision. Hold.

reports.headline: Tanker strikes remain central risk; late retaliation claims unverified
reports.text: AP and Reuters September 5 attribute three tanker strikes to CENTCOM following alleged missile attacks on US warships. Oil-fleet threat reconfirmed. Late Iranian retaliation headlines await independent damage verification; no new signal.

reports.headline: Capital-specific restraint is not a nationwide Ukraine ceasefire
reports.text: Al Jazeera/AFP September 5 confirms Moscow talks and capital-specific three-day strike restraint, with Kyiv visit expected September 6. Reuters late headline says useful talks without breakthrough; body not retrieved. Not a nationwide ceasefire.

reports.headline: IAEA Board meets September 7-11; referral not yet adopted
reports.text: IAEA official index confirms regular September 7-11 Board meeting. Referral draft remains a proposal, not adoption. No newly verified enrichment or test threshold; existing access-denial signal carried, not freshly verified.

reports.headline: Yemen offensive threatens approaches, not verified strait closure
reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 describes government air attacks and Houthi push toward al-Makha/Bab al-Mandeb. Territorial gains and casualty totals attributed/contested. Truce-breach signal reconfirmed; no verified effective strait closure.

reports.headline: Ali al-Taher control remains an Israeli claim
reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 details Israeli claim of operational control of Ali al-Taher ridge; extent remains uncertain. A proposed wider buffer zone is not a verified new deployment. Hold. The report describes continuing operations despite the June ceasefire: ceasefire violation remains evidenced.

reports.headline: NATO hybrid warning does not establish nuclear alert
reports.text: Reuters confirms US NATO envoy support for national responses to hybrid attacks. Submarine-defence exercise reporting is not evidence of a nuclear alert or nuclear-use threat.

reports.headline: Capital-only strike pause accompanies US envoy talks
reports.text: AP full report: Putin met Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow September 5; Kyiv visit planned Sunday. Both sides agreed to a limited pause on strikes against the two capitals through Monday, not a nationwide ceasefire. Existing diplomatic signal reconfirmed. Hold.

reports.headline: Government air operations intensify near Red Sea approaches
reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 full report describes government air attacks September 4 and continued Houthi offensive toward al-Makha and Bab al-Mandeb. Counts and casualties are attributed; territorial gains contested. Existing truce-breach signal reconfirmed; no proof of strait closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Tanker strikes and oil-fleet warning remain central risk
reports.text: AP full report confirms CENTCOM says it struck three Iranian tankers and threatened the oil fleet after alleged missile attacks on US warships. Already reflected in prior scan; damage and sequence remain military claims. Hold.

reports.headline: IAEA confirms September 7-11 Board meeting; referral remains proposal
reports.text: Official IAEA advisory confirms regular Board meeting September 7-11. AP indexed September 4 report describes a proposed Iran referral resolution, not adoption. Reuters September 1 extraction lacks article body. No new technical threshold verified. Hold.

reports.headline: NATO envoy stresses national responses to hybrid threats
reports.text: Reuters full report quotes US NATO envoy on national responses to hybrid attacks and protection of critical infrastructure. Submarine-defence headlines do not establish a nuclear alert. Hold.

reports.headline: Cooperation agreement is not proof of arms delivery
reports.text: Reuters confirms Vietnam-Myanmar agreement on training, exchanges, rescue and security cooperation. Not verified new combat materiel or battlefield support delivery. Hold.

reports.headline: US acknowledges tanker strikes; oil-fleet threat is now explicit
reports.text: AP and Reuters on September 5 report CENTCOM acknowledging strikes on three Iranian tankers after missile attacks on US warships. AP quotes an explicit threat to destroy the oil fleet. reports.headline: US NATO envoy warns against hybrid attacks; response remains primarily national

sources: Bangkok Post / Thai Examiner / Pattani Police / ISOC Region 4 (30 August source event)

reports.headline: Sudan buildup signal expires after configured decay window
reports.text: The configured 72-hour window for sudan:military_buildup expired. The Yale satellite assessment and 31 August UN briefing remain material conflict evidence, but no fresh qualifying force-buildup report renewed the signal in the scan window. Sudan returns 100→94 and remains IMMINENT.
sources: Yale Humanitarian Research Lab / regional reporting (30 August source event)
United Nations Office of the Spokesperson (31 August corroboration)

reports.headline: Myanmar strike signal expires after configured decay window
reports.text: The configured 72-hour decay window for myanmar:infrastructure_strike expired without a fresh qualifying strike report in the past-24-hour deep scan. The 31 August Shwegu reporting remains historically relevant, but it no longer supports an active signal. Risk returns 35→30 and remains CRITICAL.
sources: Burma News International / Kachin News Group (31 August source event)

reports.headline: Iran says U.S. strike hit Sirik wedding, killing five
reports.text: Reuters and Al Jazeera reported that Iranian authorities said a U.S. strike in Sirik hit a wedding gathering and killed five people, including a child. The casualty claim remains attributed to Iran, but the strike is part of the independently confirmed U.S.-Iran exchange and reconfirms the canonical ceasefire_violation signal. Iran conventional is already capped at 100/IMMINENT, so no numeric increase is applied.

reports.headline: U.S. and Iran complete their largest exchange of strikes in weeks
reports.text: Reuters reported that U.S. Central Command completed a new strike wave against IRGC air-defence, radar, maritime, mine-laying and communications targets, while Iran struck back at U.S. assets in Jordan, Bahrain and Iraq. The exchange was the most serious escalation in weeks and reconfirms ceasefire_violation; continued Hormuz restrictions reconfirm hormuz_closed. The tracker is already capped at 100/IMMINENT, so no numeric increase is applied.

reports.headline: UN SECURITY COUNCIL SET FOR SEPTEMBER VOTE ON IRAN SANCTIONS MONITORING
reports.text: France said the Security Council is expected to vote on 17 September on renewing the Iran sanctions-monitoring panel; Russia and China oppose the oversight mechanism. This procedural showdown did not cross any configured technical, inspection, treaty, detonation or emergency threshold. Hold Iran nuclear at 75 raw / 82 coupled, IMMINENT.

reports.headline: IAEA access denied at more than 20 Iranian nuclear sites
reports.text: A fresh IAEA quarterly report says Iran is refusing access to more than 20 nuclear sites and that inspectors cannot verify enriched-uranium stocks. Reuters and DPA independently reported the finding. This activates the canonical iaea_access_denied signal; no enrichment-to-90%, nuclear-test, Fordow-activation or NPT-withdrawal threshold was verified.

reports.headline: Two Saudi supertankers struck minutes apart in Strait of Hormuz
reports.text: CBC and Associated Press reporting identifies two Saudi supertankers struck about 12 minutes apart in the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO incident reporting and the continuing restrictions reconfirm hormuz_closed and ceasefire_violation; the conventional tracker remains capped at 100.

reports.headline: Iran official-warning indicator expires without fresh qualifying confirmation
reports.text: The 29 August Iranian military-command statement has crossed the configured temporal-decay floor. The 16-call deep scan found no fresh qualifying official adoption or technical, inspection, treaty or detonation threshold. The configured official-rhetoric indicator clears and risk falls 73→68 raw / 80→76 coupled, remaining IMMINENT.
sources: AFP via L'Orient Today (29 August source event)

reports.headline: Trump says renewed U.S.-Iran strikes are unlikely to become a major escalation
reports.text: The Washington Post reports that U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States might continue limited military action against Iran but suggested the renewed exchange of strikes was unlikely to become a major escalation. This moderates the latest rhetoric but is not a verified negotiating process and does not change a configured signal. Iran conventional risk holds 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Tanker hit by three projectiles as visible Hormuz traffic falls to five vessels a day
reports.text: Reuters reporting carried by The Business Times says Kpler counted only five visible commodity-vessel transits per day through Hormuz over the weekend. UKMTO said a tanker leaving the strait was struck by three projectiles; no casualties or environmental impact were reported. Brent reached $91.05 and WTI $86.59 at 0044 GMT. The event reconfirms the existing Hormuz closure and kinetic-breach conditions but does not justify a probability increase above the 100 cap.

reports.headline: UN reports nearly 60 civilians killed across Ukraine over the weekend
reports.text: The UN spokesperson said Ukrainian authorities reported nearly 60 civilians killed and 240 injured across the country over the weekend, including 38 killed after a drone strike on an ammunition depot triggered a major explosion in the Kyiv region. The official humanitarian summary corroborates the sustained high-tempo campaign and reconfirms russia_ukraine:military_buildup, but the tracker remains capped at 99/IMMINENT.
sources: United Nations Office of the Spokesperson

reports.headline: UN says escalating Sudan fighting displaced about 22,000 people in Blue Nile
reports.text: The UN spokesperson said local authorities estimated that escalating fighting in Geissan displaced nearly 22,000 people in seven days. The same briefing reported casualties from attacks and drone strikes around El Obeid, a lethal drone strike near the Chad border and renewed displacement from fighting in South Kordofan. This corroborates sustained conflict severity but does not independently establish a new canonical signal beyond Sudan’s already active military_buildup; risk remains capped at 100/IMMINENT.
sources: United Nations Office of the Spokesperson

reports.headline: Man shot dead near Kenya-Somalia border; motive remains unverified
reports.text: Hiiraan Online reports that unidentified attackers killed a man travelling to morning prayers in Lafey Sub-County near the Kenya-Somalia border. Police opened an investigation, but no attacker, motive, al-Shabaab link, infrastructure damage or operational force package was verified. The incident is logged as a watch item; Kenya-Somalia border risk holds 25/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Lebanese speaker warns of existential risk while implementation diplomacy continues
reports.text: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

reports.headline: Kyiv enters fifth day of near-continuous alerts as Russia expands jet-drone attacks
reports.text: The Kyiv Independent reports a fifth consecutive day of near-continuous alerts in Kyiv as Russia increases jet-powered drone attacks; Ukrainian regional authorities reported at least seven people killed and 45 injured elsewhere over the preceding day. The operational tempo reconfirms military_buildup, but it adds no separate configured transition. Russia-Ukraine risk holds 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Polish fighters intercept Russian Il-20 over Baltic without airspace breach
reports.text: Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Polish fighters intercepted a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance aircraft over the Baltic about 30 km from Poland. He said no Polish airspace violation occurred. The encounter is an allied-readiness watch item, not a new configured Russia threshold; raw/coupled risk holds 70/80.

reports.headline: Lebanon speaker rejects buffer zone while U.S.-brokered framework remains active
reports.text: Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri rejected a buffer zone or security belt and opposed negotiations under fire. Shafaq reported that seven U.S.-brokered rounds have produced no tangible progress, but the June framework and future negotiating path remain in force. The statement reconfirms diplomacy_refused while diplomacy_active remains active; raw/displayed risk holds 99/100.

reports.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least five Palestinians in Gaza City
reports.text: Al Jazeera reports that two Israeli attacks killed at least five Palestinians in Gaza City, including three people killed when a drone-fired missile struck a vehicle in Tel al-Hawa. The attacks reconfirm ceasefire_violation; Israel-Palestine risk holds 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Hague panel tells India to honor Indus Waters Treaty pending hydro review
reports.text: The Washington Post and regional reporting say an arbitration panel ordered India to suspend disputed hydroelectric work and comply with the Indus Waters Treaty while review continues. The legal channel is stabilizing but does not establish a configured diplomacy_active threshold; India risk holds 15/ELEVATED.

reports.headline: UAE intercepts Iranian drone and calls the incident a dangerous escalation
reports.text: Associated Press reporting carried by PBS says the UAE intercepted an Iranian drone approaching over its territorial waters and reported no damage. The UAE called the incident a dangerous escalation and a sovereignty violation, while a presidential adviser called for a political solution and normal Hormuz navigation. The incident reconfirms the existing kinetic-breach condition; the political appeal alone is not a verified negotiating process.

reports.headline: Myanmar junta launches heavy Shwegu airstrikes after resistance seizes supply vessel
reports.text: Burma News International and Kachin News Group report repeated airstrikes after KIA/PDF forces damaged and seized a vessel from a 15-ship military supply flotilla. A local estimate of 60–70 bombs in one day was not independently verified. The event reconfirms infrastructure_strike; Myanmar risk holds 35/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Russia reports strategic ICBM launch and missile-force mobility exercise
reports.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said a solid-fuel ICBM launched from Plesetsk reached the Kura test site and that Strategic Missile Forces conducted a mobile-system exercise. The missile type was not identified. The event is a strategic-posture watch item, not an official nuclear-use threat or configured Russia signal; raw/coupled risk holds 70/80.

reports.headline: Thailand confirms late-September BRN peace round focused on safety zones
reports.text: Thai chief peace negotiator Thanut Suvarnananda said a formal round with the same BRN delegation is planned in Malaysia and will focus on reducing violence and possible safety zones. The scheduled facilitated process activates diplomacy_active while the Pattani bombing keeps infrastructure_strike active; risk falls 37→34/CRITICAL.
sources: Thai chief peace negotiator Thanut Suvarnananda

reports.headline: Taiwan says China is tightening air-sea control around the island
reports.text: Reuters reports Taiwan's annual defence review says Beijing is strengthening control of nearby air and sea space and centering exercises on joint blockade/control, while the report says China still lacks the capability for an amphibious assault. No fresh blockade order or attack was verified; raw/coupled risk holds 24/29.

reports.headline: UN nuclear-test session renews disarmament warning without an operational escalation
reports.text: UN News reports that the General Assembly marked the International Day against Nuclear Tests and heard warnings against any resumption of explosive testing. The event is a normative disarmament signal, not evidence of a nuclear test, force movement or new safeguards emergency; no configured tracker changes.

reports.headline: Spain says no evidence Morocco orchestrated the Ceuta migration surge
reports.text: Spanish authorities found no evidence that Morocco directed the Ceuta surge, according to reporting on the prime minister's assessment. The finding weakens external-orchestration claims but does not itself activate a configured diplomatic signal; risk holds 27/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Yemeni forces report seizure of Iranian drone components bound for Houthis
reports.text: Yemen's government-aligned National Resistance Forces said naval units intercepted Iranian-made drone components in the Red Sea en route to the Houthis. Anadolu Agency, Yemen Online and The Arab Weekly carried the claim, but their accounts trace to the same force spokesman; promised footage and component provenance were not independently verified, and Iran and the Houthis did not comment. external_backing remains inactive pending independent material or imagery verification; yemen_red_sea holds 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Russian State Duma deputy explicitly urges tactical nuclear use against Ukraine
reports.text: State Duma deputy and Rodina leader Alexei Zhuravlev said Russia was obliged to use tactical nuclear weapons to force Ukraine to capitulate. His public Telegram channel carried the statement and Kyiv Post documented the quote and role. This clears nuclear_rhetoric_official for the Russia-NATO tracker, but it is not an executive order or evidence of imminent use. Raw/coupled risk rises 70→72 / 80→82.

reports.headline: Civil-society groups warn of escalating Twic-Abyei threats and ultimatum
reports.text: Eye Radio reports two peacebuilding groups warned of hostile propaganda, direct threats and a reported seven-day displacement ultimatum in the Twic-Abyei dispute. They urged presidential and UN intervention. No fresh clash or force mobilization was verified; risk holds 19/ELEVATED.

reports.headline: North Korea vows to strengthen nuclear force amid allied-drill dispute
reports.text: Reuters reports North Korea said U.S. hostility remains unchanged and vowed to strengthen its nuclear force. The rhetoric is escalatory but the tracker has no configured rhetoric signal; no fresh missile_range_test or nuclear_test was verified and risk holds 24/ELEVATED.

reports.headline: Libyan rival delegations sign UN-sponsored two-year election path
reports.text: Western and eastern Libyan delegations signed a draft final agreement at UNSMIL headquarters covering elections within 24 months, election-commission restructuring and unified institutions. Legislative approval remains unresolved, but the formal implementation step activates diplomacy_active and lowers risk 27→24/ELEVATED.

reports.headline: Iran fires ballistic missiles at U.S.-used bases in Jordan after Larak strike
reports.text: Iran's IRGC said it fired ballistic missiles at King Hussein and Al-Azraq bases in Jordan after the U.S. strike on Larak Island. Jordan's military said it intercepted eight missiles that entered its airspace, and no casualties were reported. CBC, Deutsche Welle, Task & Purpose and TRT World independently carried the exchange. The response reconfirms the already-active ceasefire_violation signal for iran_conventional; it does not establish a new configured signal, and probability remains capped at 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Turkish-Somali forces free hijacked MV LUTUF; pirate death toll unverified
reports.text: Somalia's Defence Ministry says a 10-day operation freed the Cameroon-flagged cargo ship, destroyed four pirate boats and killed 14 alleged pirates. AP confirmed the vessel and crew were freed through a local elder, but the death toll and cargo details were not independently verified. Risk holds 38/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Trump threatens Iran's Kharg Island oil hub as U.S.-Iran strikes resume
reports.text: CNBC reports President Trump shared an AI-generated video depicting an attack on Kharg Island, Iran's primary oil-export terminal, and said it was 'going to be blown to smithereens.' This explicit threat activates canonical oil_infrastructure_threat. A separate uncorroborated IRGC tanker-damage claim was excluded from scoring. Iran conventional remains capped at 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island; IRGC vows retaliation
reports.text: AP and CNN report U.S. forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island after a U.S. official said Iranian forces were preparing rockets carrying sea mines toward Hormuz. Al Jazeera and the IRGC, via IRIB, report casualties and an Iranian retaliation vow. The first U.S. strike in about a month activates ceasefire_violation for iran_conventional; no actual new mine deployment was independently verified. Probability stays capped at 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Algeria deploys fighter patrols to support Niger after failed mutiny
reports.text: Algeria's Defence Ministry said two fighter patrols were dispatched on a support mission requested by Niger; official Algerian reporting and independent coverage identify four Su-30 fighters with transport and aerial-refuelling support. The verified foreign military deployment activates external_backing for mali_sahel. Risk rises 40→44/CRITICAL; the event maps to the existing Central Sahel tracker rather than a new zone.

reports.headline: AP confirms 47 killed in Kenscoff gang attack as Haiti holds funerals
reports.text: Associated Press reports hundreds attended funerals after the 23 August Kenscoff attack killed 47 people; the UN Human Rights Office said about 150 heavily armed gang members participated. This is stronger confirmation of the prior event, not a new configured signal transition; haiti_gang_conflict holds 30/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Fresh bombing and demolitions expand across southern Lebanon
reports.text: Lebanon's NNA, Türkiye Today, Arab News and L'Orient Today report a large bombing in Houla plus demolitions of an elderly-care home and other buildings. The activity reconfirms ceasefire violation while diplomacy active remains supported by continuing talks; israel_lebanon holds 95 raw / 100 coupled.

reports.headline: Nigerian troops repel coordinated Kukawa attack; army says 26 attackers killed
reports.text: The Nigerian Army said troops repelled a coordinated attack on Kukawa in Borno, killing 26 attackers while four soldiers were wounded. Channels Television, Premium Times, TheCable and other outlets carried the statement. No new configured signal is assigned; nigeria_insurgency holds 30/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: U.S. military leaders warn prolonged Iran operations are straining wider readiness
reports.text: The Washington Post reports that several U.S. military leaders advised the defense secretary that extending large-scale Iran operations is unsustainable and would weaken capabilities elsewhere. The Wall Street Journal separately reports that Middle East transfers left some Patriot PAC-3 and ATACMS inventories in Europe beyond critical. This is a material allied-readiness constraint, not a verified withdrawal order or a new configured threshold; probabilities hold.

reports.headline: Iran says Hormuz closed while mediators pursue a conditional shipping route
reports.text: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the Strait of Hormuz is closed and vessels seeking passage must coordinate with Iran; Reuters separately described the unresolved conflict as keeping the strait closed. Kpler still counted seven commodity-vessel crossings on Thursday, so this is a general closure with selective passage rather than zero traffic. Oman, Qatar and Pakistan remain engaged in mediation, but no route has been implemented.

reports.headline: Reuters: Israeli strike kills two Palestinians, including a 3-year-old child, in central Gaza
reports.text: Reuters reports that an Israeli airstrike near a bakery in Deir Al-Balah killed two Palestinians, including a three-year-old child, and wounded several others. Gaza health officials supplied the casualty account; the Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas militant without giving further detail. This reconfirms the already-active ceasefire_violation indicator; israel_palestine holds 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Russia says preparations began for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy system
reports.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said it had begun preparations for massive strikes against Ukraine's energy facilities. POLITICO, NBC News and multiple outlets reported the announcement. The declared operational preparation clears the configured military buildup threshold; russia_ukraine remains capped at 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Yale satellite assessment finds major military buildup at Ethiopia base near Sudan front
reports.text: Yale HRL assessed roughly 100 new light military vehicles, 15 armoured-personnel-carrier-like vehicles and fresh logistics at Ethiopia's Asosa base, warning this could support 750–1,000 personnel and an imminent RSF attack on Ad-Damazin. Eastleigh Voice, Addis Standard and Ahram carried the findings. military_buildup activates; sudan rises 94→100.

reports.headline: Oil ends the week lower as Hormuz-deal rumours circulate
reports.text: A 30 August market wrap reports Friday settlements of Brent at $89.31 and WTI at $83.40, down more than 5% and 4% respectively for the week, while unresolved Hormuz transit disruption remains an upside risk. The report cites market rumours, not a signed shipping agreement; iran_conventional remains 100/IMMINENT with no configured signal change.

reports.headline: Armed insurgents seize Pattani department store and detonate three bombs
reports.text: Bangkok Post and Thai Examiner report five armed insurgents seized Pattani's Global House, evacuated civilians, detonated three bombs and left a nearly 50 kg booby trap for responders. Police and ISOC Region 4 supplied details. This clears the configured infrastructure strike threshold; southern_thailand rises 32→37.

reports.headline: Myanmar military gains ground through airpower, conscription and external pressure
reports.text: Al Jazeera reports that Myanmar's military has retaken 22 of 101 towns lost after the coup, while analysts cite mass conscription, sustained airpower and Chinese pressure on armed groups. The report describes a cumulative strategic shift, not a fresh event inside the configured 72-hour military_buildup window; the tracker holds at 35%.

reports.headline: North Korea replaces defence minister in wider military leadership reshuffle
reports.text: KCNA says Defence Minister No Kwang Chol was dismissed and demoted, Kim Song Gi was appointed, and several other senior officers were promoted. State media also claimed unspecified advances in new combat weapon systems, but no fresh missile launch or nuclear test was reported; the tracker holds at 24%.

reports.headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza hospital compound as other attacks kill four
reports.text: AFP reports that Israel said it targeted a Hamas commander in a storage structure at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, causing four minor injuries and material damage; Gaza civil defence reported four deaths in separate strikes. The event reconfirms the active ceasefire_violation signal without moving the 99% ceiling.

reports.headline: Russia sustains 28-hour combined strike series against Ukraine
reports.text: ISW says Russia launched more than 550 drones and loitering munitions plus an unspecified number of missiles during a strike series lasting over 28 hours on 28–29 August, primarily targeting Kyiv. The campaign reconfirms extreme battlefield escalation but does not create a new configured signal; russia_ukraine remains at 99%.
sources: Institute for the Study of War

reports.headline: Finland's president sees no evidence Russia will risk attacking NATO
reports.text: Reuters and Anadolu report Finnish President Alexander Stubb said he sees no evidence Russia is likely to attack NATO, citing alliance deterrence while warning allies not to lower readiness. No configured signal changes; Russia-NATO holds 70 raw / 80 coupled.

reports.headline: Regional officials meet to strengthen Red Sea and Gulf of Aden maritime security
reports.text: Hiiraan Online reports officials from Somalia, Ethiopia, Yemen and Djibouti met in Nairobi to strengthen maritime law enforcement in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. The meeting is a mitigating watch item, but it is not a conflict-party settlement and does not activate a configured signal; somalia_gulf_of_aden holds 38/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Kim Jong Un says North Korea could destroy South Korea if threatened
reports.text: News On AIR reports Kim Jong Un said North Korea could destroy South Korea if its security were threatened. The statement raises rhetorical temperature ahead of the 7-11 September trilateral exercise, but no fresh missile_range_test or nuclear_test was verified; north_korea holds 24/ELEVATED.

reports.headline: Turkish and Somali forces free vessel seized by pirates
reports.text: Somalia’s defence ministry says Turkish and Somali forces freed the hijacked MV LUTUF. The vessel recovery is a mitigating development, but the wider piracy cluster remains active and no configured signal changes; somalia_gulf_of_aden holds 38/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Fresh Gaza attacks reported as ceasefire violations continue
reports.text: TRT World reports fresh Israeli attacks in Gaza under a ceasefire it says remains in effect, including a strike on a delivery-company e-bike whose victim was brought to Al Shifa Hospital. The reporting reconfirms the already-active ceasefire_violation indicator; no implemented settlement or new configured force threshold was verified, so risk holds 99.

reports.headline: Israeli troops raise flag on Lebanese building amid continued southern military activity
reports.text: Middle East Monitor, citing Anadolu reporting and imagery, says Israeli troops raised a flag on a Lebanese-owned building under construction in Kfar Chouba while strikes, shelling and demolitions continued elsewhere in the south. The event reconfirms the existing ceasefire_violation indicator; negotiations remain active and risk holds 95 raw / 100 coupled.

reports.headline: Haiti gang releases women and children after mass kidnapping
reports.text: Associated Press reporting syndicated by the Los Angeles Times says six children and seven women were released after a gang kidnapped more than 50 people during the deadly Kenscoff attack. The partial release is mitigating but does not end the attack pattern or activate a configured signal; haiti_gang_conflict holds 30/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Ukraine says Russian planners were tasked to prepare possible Kyiv and Chernihiv offensives
reports.text: POLITICO reports that Ukraine says it has verified intelligence that Russian military chiefs were tasked to plan and prepare possible ground attacks on Kyiv and Chernihiv. The same official said there is not yet evidence of Russian troops gathering for the attacks. This is a serious watch item, but it does not clear the configured military_buildup threshold; Russia–Ukraine risk holds 99.
sources: Office of the President of Ukraine (attributed)

reports.headline: Hezbollah chief rejects Lebanon-Israel framework and demands cancellation
reports.text: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem publicly rejected the signed framework, called it illegal and demanded its cancellation. A further negotiating round is still expected in September. The explicit refusal activates diplomacy_refused while diplomacy_active and ceasefire_violation remain active; raw risk rises 95→99 and coupling keeps the displayed value at 100.

reports.headline: Iran and Oman discuss a Hormuz traffic plan excluding military vessels
reports.text: Associated Press reports that Iran and Oman are discussing temporary commercial routes through Iranian and Omani waters while excluding military vessels. The proposal reconfirms controlled, non-normal passage and an active diplomatic channel; it does not establish total closure, renewed mining or a fresh force package.

reports.headline: European report rejects claims of a near-term Russian military threat to NATO
reports.text: Google News RSS indexed a Kyiv Post headline saying Europe rejected reports of a Russian military threat to NATO. The article body was not retrievable and no matching NATO release, allied combat step, collective-defence action or nuclear-posture change appeared in reachable official feeds. It is logged as a single-source watch item only; Russia–NATO risk holds.
sources: Kyiv Post via Google News RSS

reports.headline: Saudi delegation concludes Baghdad security talks
reports.text: Google News RSS indexed a New Arab report that a Saudi delegation concluded security talks in Baghdad. No direct article body or official readout was retrievable, so the agenda, implementation and relevance to Iraq’s militia or external-strike risk could not be verified. The item remains a diplomatic watch lead and does not change the Iraq assessment.
sources: The New Arab via Google News RSS

reports.headline: Live index says 82 ships were rerouted under Iran blockade as trade fell
reports.text: Iran International’s live Google News index said U.S. officials reported 82 ships rerouted under Iran’s blockade while Tehran reported a 35% trade decline. The article body and underlying official statements were not retrievable. The headline is consistent with heavily restricted but nonzero Hormuz passage already in the assessment; it does not establish a new closure, mine-laying event, infrastructure strike or force package.
sources: Iran International via Google News RSS

reports.headline: Iranian military-command spokesman explicitly calls for a nuclear deterrent
reports.text: Ebrahim Zolfaghari, spokesman for Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, wrote that Iran needs nuclear weapons to deter Israel. AFP/L'Orient Today and Kurdistan24 carried the statement. It is not a formal doctrine change or evidence of weaponization, but it activates nuclear_rhetoric_official and raises Iran nuclear risk 68→73 raw / 76→80 coupled.

reports.headline: Russian drone strike on warehouse west of Kyiv kills at least 37
reports.text: Associated Press directly reports a Russian drone attack on a warehouse west of Kyiv killed at least 37 people, making it the war's deadliest attack this year. The mass-casualty strike reconfirms severe escalation but does not independently clear a new configured signal; russia_ukraine holds 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Lebanese state media reports a new Israeli strike in south Lebanon
reports.text: Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported that the IDF targeted Nabatieh al-Fouqa on 29 August. The report describes fresh strikes despite the ceasefire and therefore reconfirms the already-active kinetic-breach indicator; it does not justify a duplicate probability increase.
sources: Lebanese National News Agency via Breaking The News

reports.headline: Niger defence ministry says soldiers attempted a mutiny in Niamey
reports.text: DW, Reuters and AFP report that soldiers attacked sensitive sites, targeted the airport/military base and presidential perimeter, and took soldiers hostage. Niger's defence ministry said control was being restored. The event is tracked under mali_sahel but does not yet establish a sustained military_buildup threshold; risk holds 40.

reports.headline: Fresh Gaza and West Bank airstrikes kill eight as the ceasefire remains fragile
reports.text: Associated Press reporting said Israeli strikes killed five people in Gaza and three in Jenin on 28 August. Israel's military confirmed the Gaza strikes but said it was unaware of the Khan Younis strike; it said the Jenin strike targeted a Hamas operative and two accomplices. The report reconfirms the already-active ceasefire_violation indicator without a second probability increment.
sources: Israeli military and Palestinian health officials (attributed)

reports.headline: Suspected Pakistani drones trigger high alert and searches along India’s Line of Control
reports.text: Indian reporting described suspected Pakistani drone activity over the Poonch-Rajouri sector, an army high alert and a search operation. Multiple domestic outlets carried the sightings, but no official attribution, weapons release, casualties or sustained operational force package was established. The item remains a watch signal and does not activate military_buildup.

reports.headline: Niger-overseen prisoner swap and Algerian mediation open a live channel in Mali
reports.text: Al Jazeera, citing AFP and regional security sources, reported that Tuareg rebels freed about 60 Malian soldiers in exchange for FLA figure Inkinane Ag Attaher, with Niger overseeing the exchange and Algeria helping mediate further releases. Fighting continues and Bamako still rules out talks with groups it labels terrorists, but the implemented swap and active mediation clear the configured diplomacy_active threshold. Mali risk falls 43→40.

reports.headline: BBC documents a renewed Somali piracy surge around the Gulf of Aden
reports.text: BBC reporting says at least 13 vessels have been attacked this year and three were hijacked in a recent week. It also reports disputed allegations of Turkish drone strikes near a pirate-held vessel and an unverified concentration of six warships. The piracy trend is material, but no configured threshold is activated pending firmer attribution and operational confirmation.
sources: attributed regional and Turkish official sources

reports.headline: Single-source report claims Iranian missiles targeted Dimona and Arad near Israel’s Negev nuclear complex
reports.text: India’s public broadcaster News On AIR indexed a report that Iran fired missiles toward Dimona and Arad, near the Negev Nuclear Research Center. No independent same-event confirmation, impact assessment, operational detail or official Israeli notice was retrieved in the fallback scan. The claim is logged as a critical watch item only; iran_conventional is already capped at 100 and no canonical signal changes.
sources: News On AIR via Google News RSS

reports.headline: UN and public reporting document fresh Gaza deaths and destroyed aid supplies
reports.text: UN News said Israeli attacks killed four children and destroyed humanitarian aid supplies in Gaza on 28 August; Arab News separately reported five people killed in Gaza strikes. The reports reconfirm the active kinetic breach but do not establish a distinct force package or implemented settlement.

reports.headline: UN Security Council meets as deadly Haiti gang attacks spike
reports.text: UN News reported an emergency Security Council meeting over a deadly spate of gang attacks and illicit-weapons flows. Al Jazeera and NBC reported that the already-documented Kenscoff attack killed 47 and abducted more than 50; this reinforces severity without establishing a separate new attack wave.

reports.headline: Western officials assess Russia seeks to avoid direct NATO war despite harsher rhetoric
reports.text: BBC reporting says Western officials believe Moscow wants to avoid direct military confrontation with NATO, while expecting continued cyber, sabotage and other hybrid activity and warning that miscalculation could still trigger confrontation. No new allied combat step, operational Russian strike order or official nuclear threshold was reported.

reports.headline: Hormuz traffic edges higher but remains below its 10-day average
reports.text: Kpler data reported by The Daily Star counted 10 visible commodity-vessel transits on 27 August, up from eight but below the roughly 15-vessel 10-day average. Iran and Oman were still working on corridor details. This reconfirms restricted but nonzero passage and ongoing diplomacy, not full reopening.

reports.headline: Fresh southern Lebanon strikes and Hezbollah rejection keep truce risk elevated
reports.text: UN reporting and fresh indexed coverage described continuing Israeli strikes in south Lebanon. A later Times of Israel headline said Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem again rejected the proposed Lebanon-Israel deal and refused surrender; without a retrieved formal proposal or cancelled negotiating round, the item is a watch rather than a new diplomacy_refused activation.

reports.headline: Board of Peace envoy warns failures on Gaza roadmap could collapse the ceasefire
reports.text: Nikolay Mladenov told Al Jazeera that failures by both sides to adhere to the roadmap threaten the Gaza ceasefire, while saying advance elements of an international stabilization force should arrive soon. The report also described continued Israeli raids and attacks. It reconfirms the already-active kinetic-breach and diplomatic-process indicators without a separate probability increment.

reports.headline: IAEA chief says Iran retains 440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium as access limits persist
reports.text: Scripps News directly quoted IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi saying Iran retains about 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60% and many technical capabilities. sources: The Korea Times via Google News RSS

reports.headline: Further reporting describes U.S.-supported Hormuz oil-shipping corridor

This corroborates controlled, non-zero passage but does not verify normal reopening, zero traffic, mining or a fresh infrastructure strike. Iran conventional risk holds 95 raw / 100 coupled.
sources: Khaama Press via Google News RSS

reports.text: Anadolu and Asharq Al-Awsat report overnight Israeli airstrikes, artillery fire and explosions in southern Lebanon. The fresh kinetic activity reconfirms the already-active ceasefire_violation context; it does not create an additional score at the ceiling. Israel-Lebanon risk holds 95 raw / 100 coupled.
sources: Anadolu Ajansı via Google News RSS
Asharq Al-Awsat via Google News RSS

reports.headline: Trump says no Iran talks are taking place or scheduled
